title: Jacob, Called Israel
lead: Isaac's younger twin son, who took his brother Esau's birthright and blessing, served his uncle Laban twenty years, wrestled with God at the Jabbok and was renamed Israel. His twelve sons became the tribes of Israel, and the prophets and the New Testament use his life as a mirror of God's grace to an undeserving people (Hosea 12:2–6; Malachi 1:2; Romans 9:10–13).

sections.b: Genesis tells Jacob's story from his birth (25:19–26) to his death in Egypt (49:33). The prophets recall him: Hosea uses his heel-grabbing and his wrestling as a call to repentance (Hosea 12:2–6), and Isaiah addresses the exiles as "Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen" (Isaiah 41:8; 44:1–2). "The God of Jacob" becomes a favorite title in the Psalms (Psalm 46:7; 146:5). In the New Testament, Jesus names him with Abraham and Isaac at the feast of the kingdom (Matthew 8:11), and calls himself the stairway of Jacob's dream (John 1:51). Paul uses the twins to speak of God's choosing (Romans 9:10–13), and Hebrews praises Jacob's faith as he blessed Joseph's sons, "bowing in worship over the top of his staff" (Hebrews 11:21).
